items.title: Geometric supplement: Induced distance on a round unit sphere

source.edition: Self-contained geometric supplement, 2026-11-16; expanded exposition of the exact 2026-11-09 contract
source.anchor: units[0], complete statement, definitions and six proof regions in runs/20261116-sphere-distance/source-only.json
source.attribution: Original exposition of a classical round-sphere distance formula; no claim of novelty or attribution to a primary textbook theorem.

items.statement: Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with \(\dim E=n+1\), where \(n\ge1\), and let \(S=\{z\in E:\|z\|=1\}\). For the literal inclusion \(\iota:S\to E\), give a tangent vector \(v\) at \(z\) the length \(\|D\iota_z(v)\|_E\). Define \(d_S(x,y)\) as the infimum of the lengths of all \(C^1\) paths on the closed unit interval from \(x\) to \(y\), using this induced speed. For every \(x,y\in S\), including coincident and antipodal endpoints, this distance is the angle \(\arccos\langle x,y\rangle\).
assumptions: \(E\) has a real inner product and finite dimension \(n+1\); \(n\) is a positive natural number. The rank equality selects the standard \(n\)-dimensional sphere manifold model. Positive sphere dimension is used to find a tangent direction for antipodal endpoints.
\(S\) is the actual unit sphere in \(E\), and both endpoints are arbitrary points of \(S\). No distinctness or nonantipodality hypothesis is imposed.

The tangent length is induced by the actual differential of the inclusion into \(E\). It is not a default chart-coordinate norm. The sphere retains its inherited chord metric as a topological subtype; no metric instance is replaced.

The infimum ranges over \(C^1\) paths on the closed unit interval with the prescribed endpoints. The formal distance is an extended nonnegative real and path length is a lower integral; the equality proves that the value is finite.

All differentiability and integrability of the constructed paths, and the scalar norm law needed by the path-length API, are proved internally. There is no supplied path, geodesic, derivative bound, length estimate, or additional measure structure among the theorem hypotheses.

obligations.label: Exact distance for every pair of unit sphere points

bindings.boundary: This identifies the induced length distance of a positive-dimensional unit sphere. It leaves the ambient chord metric unchanged; for antipodal points these two distances are \(2\) and \(\pi\). The condition \(n>0\) is essential for arbitrary endpoint pairs: the two-point sphere has no continuous internal path between its two distinct points. It supplies no global Riemannian bundle instance, general manifold geodesic-existence theorem, transport estimate, stochastic result, or textbook chapter completion. Spherical transport is a possible consumer of the distance identity.

assumption_deltas.reason: The rank Fact selects the chart model; positivity is the genuine source condition for arbitrary antipodal endpoint pairs.

assumption_deltas.source: Lengths are induced by the differential of the literal sphere inclusion.
assumption_deltas.reason: Explicitly retains the induced metric and does not substitute a default tangent-coordinate or chord norm.

assumption_deltas.source: Infimum of C1 path lengths, asserted equal to a finite nonnegative real angle.

assumption_deltas.reason: Extended nonnegative encoding preserves the claimed finite value; smoothness, integrability, and ENormSMulClass are constructed inside the proof.
